paragraphs: This release introduced the core security features that define Pass Vault.
Credentials can now be stored locally using encrypted storage and protected behind biometric authentication, bringing the app much closer to its original vision.
Alongside these improvements, several usability refinements helped make the overall experience feel more polished and reliable.

note.title: Dev note
content: For a long time, Pass Vault was mostly structure, navigation and ideas.
This was the release where the product finally started delivering on its promise. Seeing credentials securely encrypted and unlocked with biometrics felt like a major milestone for the project.

paragraphs: This release marked the beginning of Pass Vault as a real product.
Core navigation, settings, reusable UI components and the first credential management flows were introduced, creating a complete and usable experience for the first time.
Many of the systems added in this version would become the foundation for future features and refinements.

note.title: Dev note
content: This was the first version that truly felt like a product rather than a prototype.
Many of the ideas explored during the alpha releases finally came together into a cohesive experience. Looking back, this release represents the moment Pass Vault started to find its identity.

paragraphs: The final alpha release focused on preparing Pass Vault for the next stage of development.
Build workflows were improved and local storage foundations were introduced, paving the way for future credential management features.
While the changes were mostly behind the scenes, they played an important role in the transition toward the first stable milestones.
This release marked a major turning point for Pass Vault.
A broad visual and structural revamp introduced a clearer direction for the product, improving navigation, theming and overall organization.
Many of the foundations established during this version would continue to influence future releases.

note.title: Dev note
content: Every project eventually reaches a point where it becomes necessary to stop and rethink the direction.
This release was one of those moments. Many parts of the app were revisited, simplified and reorganized to create a stronger foundation for what Pass Vault would become.

paragraphs: This release focused on making Pass Vault feel more personal.
Theme and language preferences can now be stored locally, allowing the app to adapt to each user's preferred experience.
While still an early alpha, this version introduced some of the first customization features that would remain part of the app going forward.
The second alpha focused on strengthening the project's foundations.
While there were no major user-facing features yet, this release improved the development setup and prepared the codebase for future growth.
Many of the decisions made during this phase would help shape the architecture used throughout later versions.

note.title: Dev note
content: At this stage, most of the work was happening behind the scenes.
The app was still in its infancy, but investing time in the foundations early made it much easier to move faster in the versions that followed.

paragraphs: This is where Pass Vault started.
The very first alpha focused on building the initial foundation of the app and exploring the idea of a fast, native-feeling and privacy-first password vault experience.
Even though this version was still extremely early, it marked the beginning of the product architecture, UI direction and overall experience that would shape future releases.

note.title: Dev note
content: At this point, Pass Vault was still just an idea taking shape.
The goal wasn't to build every feature at once, but to create a solid foundation and explore what the experience could become.
Looking back now, it's interesting to see how many of the ideas from this first alpha are still part of the app today.
